la:noun:odium.html:
ŏdĭum, ii, n.
odi
(syn.: simultas, inimicitia)
Lit., hatred, grudge, illwill, animosity, enmity, aversion: odium (est) ira inveterata,: in odium alicujus irruere,to become hated by him, to incur his hatred,: non publico modo sed privato etiam odio invisus atque infestus Romanis,.—Odio alicui esse, as pass. of odi (cf. odi fin.): quod viro esse odio videas, tute tibiodio habeas,to be hateful, displeasing to,: odi odioque sum Romanis,: quid faceres, si quis docuisset te ut sic odio esses mihi?: pervenire in odium Graeciae,to incur,: omnibus odio venire,to become hated,: odium est mihi cum aliquo,I am at enmity with him,: esse odio civitati,to be hateful to,: huic odio nemus est,: tibi est odio mea fistula,: quo sit in odio status rerum,: esse alicui in odio,to be hated by,: magno odio in aliquem ferri,to be greatly imbittered against,; : alicujus subire,to incur one's hatred,: gerere adversus aliquem,to bear,: quaerere,; : movere,to excite,: saturare,to sate, satisfy,: magnum odium Pompeii suscepistis,have brought upon yourselves, have incurred,: struere,to cause, raise, excite,: concitare,: exercere,; : placare,to appease,: restinguere,.—With obj. gen.: magnum me cujuspiam rei odium cepit,I have conceived a great aversion for,: suscipere odium erga aliquem,: odio habere (postclass.),to hate, et saep.: odium jejunum,on an empty stomach,.—
Ofinanim. things: odium raphanis cum vite maximum refugitque juxta satos,aversion, antipathy,; : quercus et olea tam pertinaci odio dissident,.—
Transf.
In gen., the object of hatred; hence, an offence, annoyance, disgust, said of persons or things: optume odio's,you are an offence to me, I cannot bear you,: deorum odium atque hominum,: populi odium,: Antonius, insigne odium omnium hominum vel deorum,: omnium populorum,: neque agri, neque urbis odium me umquam percipit,disgust,.—
As a quality, offensive conduct or language, importunity, insolence, vexatiousness: cum horas tres fere dixisset, odio et strepitu senatus coactus est aliquando perorare,by the disgust they expressed,: tundendo atque odio denique effecit senex,by his tiresome, incessant preaching,: cum tuo istoc odio,with your hateful, perverse conduct,; cf. ; : odio qui posset vincere regem,in insolence,.

la:verb:odio.gloss: to have an aversion towards, to hate, dislike

la:adj:odiosus.gloss: hateful, odious, vexatious, offensive, unpleasant, disagreeable, annoying, troublesome
senses: hateful, odious, vexatious, offensive, unpleasant, disagreeable, annoying, troublesome
la:adj:odiosus.html:
ŏdĭōsus, a, um, adj.
odium
,
hateful, odious, vexatious, offensive, unpleasant, disagreeable, annoying, troublesome, etc. (class.; syn.: invisus, offensus).
Of persons: odiosus mihi es,: infestum et odiosum esse alicui,; : senex,. —
Of things: dona odiosa ingrataque,: odiosa et inepta amatio,: motus odiosiores,: verbum,: odiosissima natio,: cupidis rerum talium odiosum fortasse et molestum est carere,it is vexatious, unpleasant,; .—Hence, adv.: ŏdĭōsē, in a hateful manner, odiously, vexatiously: facere,: dicere,; ; .—Sup.: odiosissime,.

la:verb:odoro.html:
ŏdōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
odor
,
to give a smell or fragrance to, to perfume a thing (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: oleo, fragro): odorant aëra fumis,: mella,: caelum sulfure,.—Hence, ŏdōrātus, a, um, P. a., that has a smell, that emits an odor; esp., sweet-smelling, fragrant: quid tibi odorato referam sudantia ligno Balsama?: cedrus,: pabula,: capilli,: comae,: nectare odorato spargit corpus,: odoratis ignibus,: Indi,in whose country sweetsmelling spices grow,: Armenii,: dux, the prince of the Parthians or Assyrians, who border on Arabia, .—Comp.: vina mustis odoratiora,.—Sup.: odoratissimi flores,.

senses: to search out, trace out, investigate
la:verb:odoror.html:
ŏdōror, ātus, 1, v. dep.
id.
,
to smell at, examine by smelling (cf. olfacio).
Lit.: pallam,.—
Transf., to smell out, detect by the scent; to scent: ibo odorans, quasi canis venaticus,: cibum,: hominem,: vultures sagacius odorantur,: bellum,.—
Trop.
To aspire to, aim at a thing, in a contemptuous sense; to snuff, as a dog: quos odorari hunc decemviratum suspicamini,.—
To search out, trace out, investigate: odorabantur omnia et pervestigabant,: quid sentiant,: quid futurum sit,: soles enim tu haec festive odorari,: pecuniam,: tu velim ex Fabio odorere,: sagacius,: odorandi vias occultas sagax,.—
To get an inkling or smattering of any thing: odoratus philosophiam,: veritatem leviter,.

to feel reluctant to, to hate to, to be loath to
la:verb:odi.html:
ōdi, ōdisse (old form of the
pres., odio: osi sunt ab odio, declinasse antiquos testis est C. Gracchus, Paul. ex Müll. From this are formed: odis,; odiant,; odiebant,; odies, Tert. adv, Marc. 4, 35; odiet,; odivi,; odientes,; ; odiendi,init. —Pass. oditur, ; : odiremur,: oderem and odere, acc. to P.—Collat. form of the perf. osus sum, C. Gracch. ap. Paul. ex Müll.; ; ; and odivit, Anton. ap. . 19, 42), v. a.
Sanscr. root badh-, strike, thrust; Gr. ὠθέω
.
To hate (class.; cf.: detestor, abominor, aversor, abhorreo); constr. with acc. of the person or thing, with inf. or absol.
With acc.: quem omnes oderunt quā viri quā mulieres,: uxor ruri est tua, quam dudum dixeras te odisse aeque atque angues,: quid enim odisset Clodium Milo,: aliquem acerbe et penitus,: lucemque odit,: vitam,: scelus est odisse parentem,: qui hominem odiit,: semper eos osi sunt, C. Gracch. ap. Paul. ex Müll.: quas (partes) Pompeius odivit, M. Anton. ap. .—
With inf.: inimicos semper osa sum obtuerier,: peccare,; cf. .—
Absol.: oderint dum metuant, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 136 Rib.); cf. Tiber. ap. : ita amare oportere, ut si aliquando esset osurus,; : neque studere neque odisse,: furialiter,: sic objurgans, quasi oderint,; —
Transf., in gen., to dislike; to be displeased or vexed at any thing: illud rus,: Persicos apparatus,: odi cum cera vacat,.—Of subjects not personal: ruta odit hiemem et umorem ac fimum,.—Esp.: se odisse,to be ill at ease, discontented,; .—Pass.: oditur ergo in hominibus innocuis etiam nomen innocuum,: si de mundo non essemus, odiremur a mundo,, n. 2 (but in class. Lat. the pass. of odi is odio esse; v. odium).

la:noun:odor.html:
ŏdor (old form ŏdos, like arbos, labos, etc., ; ; ), ōris, m.
root od-; Gr. ὄζω, ὄδωδα, ὀδμή; whence oleo, olfacio
,
a smell, scent, odor (class.; cf. fragrantia).
Lit.
In gen.: omnis odor ad supera fertur,: odorem avide trahere naribus,: florum,.—
In partic.
A pleasant odor, perfume; concr., perfumery, essences, spices (syn. odoramenta).—So mostly in plur.: sternite lectos, incendite odores,: incendere odores,; . § 77; 2, 5, 56, § 146: croceos odores Tmolus mittit,: perfusus liquidis odoribus,perfumed waters, ointments, balsams,; : corpus differtum odoribus conditur,.—Sing., : fragrans Assyrio odore domus,: ara Fumat odore,incense,.—
A disagreeable smell, a stench, stink (syn.: nidor, faetor): putidus odor ibi saepe ex sulfure et alumine. Varr L. L. 5, § 25 Müll.: cum odos aut pabuli egestas locum mutare subegerat,: camera odore foeda,: ingratos odores,: gravis,: taeter,; : malus,: intolerabili foeditatis odore,: offensus putrefacti cerebri odore,: ignis,.—
Trop., a scent, inkling, hint, presentiment, suggestion: odor suspicionis,: legum,: hominum furta odore persequi,, § 53: res fluit ad interregnum, et est non nullos odor dictaturae, B. and K. (al. 4, 16, 11): lucri bonus est odor,; cf.: Christi bonus odor sumus Deo in iis,: urbanitatis,a tincture of politeness,.

la:adj:odorus.html:
ŏdōrus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
emitting a scent or odor, odorous (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose for odoratus).
Lit.
Sweet-smelling, fragrant: flos,: arbor, i. e. myrrha,: res, Müll. dub.—Comp.: odorius,.—Sup.: nardum Syriacum odorissimum,.—
Ill-smelling, stinking (post-class.): lumen odorum Sulfure,.
Transf., that tracks by the smell, keenscented: odora canum vis (= copia odororum canum),pack of sharp-scented hounds,.

la:noun:odoratus.html:
ŏdōrātus, ūs, m.
odoror
,
a smelling, smell.
Lit. (class.), eorum jucundus non gustatus solum. sed odoratus etiam, et spectatus, .—
Transf.
The sense of smell: nihil necesse est de gustatu et odoratu loqui,: insecta habent oculos, aliqua et odoratum,.—
A smell, scent, odor which a thing gives out, .

la:adj:odorifer.html:
ŏdōrĭfer, ĕra, ĕrum, adj.
odor-fero
,
bringing or spreading odors, fragrant, odoriferous (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: panacea,: flores,.—
Producing perfumes or spices: gens odorifera, i. e. Persae,: Arabia,.—
Prop., sweet, flattering, precious: non habemus ista odorifera,: fructus sanctae religionis,.

la:adj:odibilis.html:
ŏdĭbĭlis, e, adj.
odi
,
that deserves to be hated, hateful, odious (ante- and post-class.), Poët. ap. P.: improbitate ita odibilis, ut, etc.,; : superbia,: qui procax est,: vita,: Deo,.

la:adj:odiosior.gloss: hateful, odious, vexatious, offensive, unpleasant, disagreeable, annoying, troublesome

la:noun:odoratio.html:
ŏdōrātĭo, ōnis, f.
odoror
.
Lit., a smelling, smell (very rare): qualis est haec aurium delectatio, tales sunt oculorum et tactionum et odorationum et saporum,.—
Transf., the smell, the sense of smelling: odoratio in duas nares a summo artifice divisa est,.
